body:
We need to make sure all our examples have opposites, in tests and also in random examples.

For example:

```
Moon does not orbit the sun
Elon Musk is dead
```

And so on.

Also we should have `show all` option, to show list of all examples, which if clicked be pasted to the input field, by default we should show 4 random examples (if page refreshed they should change). And we need much more examples.

Other case is that in addition to interpretations we should have alternatives. For example:

`Moon orbit the sun` (should be around 75% of correctness), and alternative should be proposed as more precise (`Moon orbit Earth, that orbit the sun`).

Also dependencies should be listed in the left, like - `Moon orbit the sun` may only be true, if `Moon exists`, and `Sun exists`, and `orbit defined as ...` and so on.

Also definitions of each part should be listed in the left sections as well as confirmations (best quoted with link to source) and refutations (also quoted with link to source).

The right section now has title `Links Network`, instead we should name it Reasoning steps, and everything inside should obey that principle. And reasoning steps should have actual order of execution based on a reasoning strategy. We need to support as much reasoning strategies as possible, so later we will start finding meta strategies - a strategies to form other strategies.

Make sure that we should select only one of interpretation in reasoning, after that we operate based on that selected interpretation. And steps should start by interpretation of largest possible phrases as actual Q/P ids in wikidata, so we start by trying to disambiguating it. Double check related code in https://github.com/link-assistant/human-language. So for example if wikidata has a term for `Elon Musk` (2 words combined) as single term it should have priority over (`Elon` and `Musk` separately), but if they also available, that should be added to a list of interpretations, which user can select from. For all these we need to do real wikidata/wikipedia requests and cache data we already accessed in local storage, so it saves between pages and so on.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).
title: More improvements to support our vision
